runs_from_this_continuation.result: All 4 gates produced plausible-looking PASS results, but the archiving step meant to give each gate a fresh world silently failed on every attempt (Move-Item file-lock errors on stage17_world.sqlite/-shm/-wal), so all 4 actually ran against the pre-existing (Combat-contaminated) world from the interrupted session, not a fresh one.
runs_from_this_continuation.root_cause: The interrupted session's own backend process (PID 14724, launched 2026-08-29T06:26:42Z) had never actually been stopped — Stop-Stage17Authority.ps1's internal Stop-Process call was failing under this session's non-interactive PowerShell context ("PowerShell is in NonInteractive mode" confirmation prompt) without surfacing as a script-level error, so every subsequent Start-Stage17Authority.ps1 call was silently failing PORT_8000_ALREADY_IN_USE, and Godot was in fact talking to the untouched original zombie backend the whole time.
runs_from_this_continuation.impact: None of the 4 results are wrong — S17-A/B1/B2 do not depend on combat/enemy state — but they were not validated against a fresh world as intended. Corrected for all subsequent gates.
runs_from_this_continuation.fix_applied: Stop-Process calls now pass -Force -Confirm:$false; ownership verified directly against authority_backend_process.json before stopping.

runs_from_this_continuation.result: Every single gate skipped with BACKEND_NOT_READY; zero Godot processes ever launched.

runs_from_this_continuation.impact: No gate results were produced or reported from this batch; nothing false was accepted.
runs_from_this_continuation.fix_applied: Stopped deleting/archiving stage17_world.sqlite between gates entirely; restart the backend process only (RESUMED boot), which both boots in seconds and lets the dev-bootstrap self-heal logic naturally rotate any defeated fixture NPCs.
